subject.title: Feature: Add denylist support for exec-approvals

question: What native exec denylist policy shape should OpenClaw accept for this security-sensitive approvals surface?
rationale: The request adds persisted security/config behavior across core runtime, gateway protocol, node host, CLI, UI, and docs, and open PRs propose different semantics that automation should not choose unilaterally.

options.title: Review direct denylist PR
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/92456 as the main candidate and require protocol, prompt-parity, docs, and live proof before merge.

options.title: Narrow to path-deny first
options.body: Land or replace https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/88075 for sensitive path reads while leaving command-content denylist policy open.

options.title: Reject native denylist mode
options.body: Close the denylist direction only if maintainers decide permissive-with-deny-exceptions is outside OpenClaw's security model.

recommendation.title: Review direct denylist PR
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/92456 as the main candidate and require protocol, prompt-parity, docs, and live proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete provided the latest maintainer-facing issue review and current blame also routes the checked-out policy/schema/docs surface through Peter Steinberger's recent commit.
